purpose: Measure per-ObsID ACIS gain intercept and slope from the Ni K-alpha and Au L-alpha lines in the original matched blank-sky cells, without opening a Bullet source PHA or fitting an astrophysical redshift.
claim_boundary: This detector-nuisance audit can quantify calibration uncertainty at the observed Fe-K energy. It cannot establish an ICM velocity, admit a Sigma source, open Abell 2146 or test gravity.

workload.background_rule: sum integer COUNTS channel-by-channel over the original non-overlapping matched blank-sky cell PHAs separately within each ObsID; do not use an ASCA-scaled combined background as the gain spectrum
workload.energy_grid_rule: require identical 1024-channel EBOUNDS within and across all admitted cells before summing

line_model.likelihood: Poisson Cash statistic on ungrouped integer counts
line_model.model_per_line: positive exponential-linear local continuum plus one bin-integrated Gaussian line
line_model.joint_gain_relation: fit the two recorded centroids independently, then transform their profile covariance exactly to E_cal_keV = intercept_keV + slope * E_recorded_keV

propagation.centroid_covariance: independent Ni/Au profile variances using the larger asymmetric Delta-Cash=1 half-width for each line
propagation.gain_covariance: Jacobian propagation from the two recorded centroids to intercept and slope
propagation.source_use: propagate the intercept/slope covariance to each source redshift likelihood; do not shift the source data in the primary branch
propagation.later_gate: after source fitting, one-sigma gain uncertainty at observed Fe-K must be at most 0.2 times the median pre-gain total redshift uncertainty

runtime.python_environment: existing Windows Python with Astropy and SciPy; frozen /home archive paths resolve through the Ubuntu-24.04 WSL UNC mount
